questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: UCSD has an institute for oceanography (Scripps Institute of Oceanography) which is an interest of mine and they are very good at climate studies. Also a great location neat the ocean with good study environments.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing place but very expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UCPH gave a very good overall guideline on how to get a visa and what needed to be done before going abroad. However, there were a lot of documents which needed to be sorted and many processes to go through in order to get a visa, health insurences and other requirements for the university. There was a lot of uncertainty regarding housing and the process of getting campus housing was long and a bit confusing but worked out in the end. All the information needed to organize the exchange was a bit stressfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not recieve any special assistance but it felt like it was available if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: International house was the most obvious housing for exchange students which consisted of shared appartments where most people had their own room. Some other on campus housing were also available.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a paid meal plan included in the rent and multiple places to acces it. It was expencive and only included one meal a day in average. There was a kitchen in all the appartments in I-house

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very expencive to live on campus or whereever you decide to live in La Jolla/San Diego. They are very strict regarding noice, parties and alcohol. The facilities are decent in the appartments but the campus is very nice. There is a lot of activities to do around campus and it is relatively close to the beach.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to make a general motivational application to get into the UC system where I had choose my preferences of universities and relevant courses. When I got accepted at UCSD I had to apply for the DS2019 to get my visa. Then I had to choose my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a guide on how to apply for each step. I also had some questions which I asked the student service who helped me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesful in registering for the classes I wanted and even though I did not have all the prerequisits for the classes I could ask for permition by the professers to get a spot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that you plan everything in good time inadvance and that you sort out your prerequisits before going. It was a bit stressfull to learn a new registration system but if you take your time it will definetly work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high level in general and the classes used more applied math and physics than what we are used to at geography at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were more assigments and test, but other than that it was simulair to UCPH with discussions and presentations. They also used teacher assistants for all classes who were very hepfull.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Physical Oceanography, Physical Basis of Global Warming, Analysis of Oceanographic and Atmospheric Data.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Ice and the Climate, Seismology, Water Pollution.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Analysis of Oceanographic and Atmospheric Data really improved my coding skills and gave taught me much about data analysis but it was VERY demanting and requires many hours of investment and struggle but in the end it was the class I learned most from and the one I perfomed best in since it was the most interesting class. I can recommend it if you are interested in earth systems, climate change and data analysis and statistics and dont mind putting in some time learning how to code. I did not have any coding experience but managed anyways by investing a lot of time.

I can also recommend Introduction to physical oceanography which gives a good understanding of the physics in the oceans.

questions.answer: The food was very expensive.

questions.answer: Food and travels.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most sports were available. There was a nice gym, climbing center, a very nice outdoor pool, tennis courts and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend the climbing club. It is great community and does not require any skill level.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go climbing with the locals in the nearby mountains or go surfing at La Jolla. There is also many good hikes nearby but it requires a car (or friends with cars...).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Nice and easygoing, friendly people and a great community for international students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most people at campus are living away from home for the first time and they are not used to manage everything in the household by them selves; cleaning, cooking etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor life and use of nature was great but you had to seek it. There are so many things to do if you seek it. I also realy appriciate a bagel and coffe on the way to class every morning :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Plan everything well in advance. Dont stress to much about classes. Remember to enjoy your stay by going on trips - there is a great acces to nature and activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: California is very car based so I would recommend buying a car to get around. Maybe you can share it with some friends. I did not have one so I relied much on my friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Passing harder classes was very rewarding and also experiencing some amazing nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was challenging adapting to a more mathematical and physical approach in the classes but also very rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
